clue.text: Eva maybe embracing second friend in my book

indicators.note: embracing means holding something in the arms, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: Eva Perón, the Argentine first lady, is an example of someone surnamed Peron
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone muses that Eva, perhaps hugging a close companion, is what they personally think of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eva maybe' points to Eva Perón, wife of the Argentine president; 'embracing' signals that her surname holds the abbreviation for second.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is so 'in my book' means it is so in one's own opinion, from a personal point of view.

clue.text: Is hotel below average for district?

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means these letters come after the first piece

parts.note: par is the normal or average standard
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about whether a lodging that is less than ordinary counts as an area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' works only because this is a down entry, so the later pieces sit under the word for average.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is a local administrative or church district, a synonym in the sense of a small area.

clue.text: Concerning drink rumour

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a business letter
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A rumour going round that concerns someone's drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A report can be hearsay or gossip passed from person to person, a synonym for a story going about.

clue.text: Six balls wife initially hooked with wood in golf — mind-boggling!

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled by one bowler

indicators.note: initially says to take only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: elm is a kind of tree and its timber
G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sporting scene mixing cricket, a hooked shot and a wooden club on the golf course, all astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is six deliveries. 'wood in golf' suggests a golf club, but the three words each give their own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overwhelming is so great it overpowers the mind, much like something staggering or astounding.

clue.text: Encourage American gamble

parts.note: a bet is a wager or gamble

explanation.surface: Someone urges a US citizen to place a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to support or urge on, usually in wrongdoing, a synonym for encouraging.

clue.text: Texts intoxicated — rue it later

definitions.note: a plural noun, standing for written works collectively, which the mass noun answer covers

indicators.note: intoxicated means drunk and confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Drunken messages sent now that the sender will regret afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Texts' suggests phone messages, but here means written works.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature is the body of written works, so it consists of texts in the scholarly sense.

clue.text: Prevent vessels returning

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for vessels is read backwards

parts.note: pots are containers or vessels

explanation.surface: An order to keep ships from coming back to port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests ships but means cooking pots.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something is to prevent it from happening, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Adolescent themes regularly annoy the Queen

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word themes is taken

parts.note: to nag is to pester or annoy
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A young person's recurring subjects irritate the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking letters 1, 3 and 5 of THEMES gives TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a youth aged thirteen to nineteen, the same as an adolescent.

clue.text: Display outside is heaven

indicators.note: outside means placed around, so the word for display surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to parade something is to show it off or display it

explanation.surface: Showing off in the open air is bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is the Garden of Eden or the abode of the blessed, a synonym for heaven.

clue.text: Means to relax, with no time to wrap gift

indicators.note: to wrap means to enclose, so the shortened word goes round the other piece
with no means without, so a letter is dropped from the word for relax

parts.note: to rest is to relax
a present is a gift

explanation.surface: Instructions for unwinding when there is no time to wrap a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no time' drops T from the word for relax, leaving RES, and 'to wrap' puts that around the gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to stand for it, as a symbol means what it signifies.

clue.text: Stomach empty, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase says the word for empty is to be heard, not read, giving a word spoken alike

parts.note: bare means empty or unfurnished, as in a bare room

explanation.surface: A belly with nothing in it, judging by the noises it makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to put up with it or tolerate it, the same as to bear it.

clue.text: So reticent in altering meeting

indicators.note: altering means changing, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone so reserved that they change at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' suggests a gathering of people, but it is where things cross.
explanation.definitionFit: An intersection is a place where roads or lines meet, a junction or crossing.

clue.text: Crafty little mammal departs

parts.note: a shrew is a tiny insect-eating mammal
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A cunning small animal makes its exit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shrewd is sharp and clever in practical matters, close in sense to crafty or astute.

clue.text: Sponge misplaced under dark English shed

indicators.note: misplaced means put in the wrong position, so the remaining letters are rearranged
shed means cast off, so a letter is dropped from the words under and dark

explanation.surface: A sponge mislaid beneath a dim English garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden building but means discard: drop E from UNDERDARK, then rearrange UNDRDARK. 'Sponge' is slang for a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is informal for someone who soaks up alcohol, a habitual drinker.

clue.text: Rags badly sewn perhaps husband's thrown out

indicators.note: badly means in a poor or disordered way, so the letters are rearranged
thrown out means removed, so a letter is dropped from the word perhaps

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Clothes stitched poorly, maybe because the husband has been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rags' suggests tattered clothes, but means cheap papers. PERHAPS loses H to give PERAPS, rearranged with SEWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag is a dismissive term for a low-quality newspaper, so rags are the papers themselves.

clue.text: Change three lenses, keeping very still

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the rearranged letters hold the abbreviation
change means alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An optician's instruction to swap three lenses while the patient stays motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like motionless but is the adverb meaning even so.
explanation.definitionFit: Still, used as an adverb, means however or all the same, matching the sense of in spite of that.

clue.text: The spread includes one ham?

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a span is the spread or extent of something, as of wings
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A buffet spread that features a single cut of ham, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like the meat but means an overacting performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is a showy, overacting performer, and an actor is called a thespian after Thespis.

clue.text: Suffering can lead to glorious work of art

parts.note: pain is suffering
a tin is a can, as of food

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so only its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Suffering may lead to great things in art, as a creative maxim.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting is a picture made with paint, one kind of work of art.

clue.text: Anxiety after nut married current leader in education

indicators.note: after means that the word for anxiety follows the other pieces

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
I is the symbol for electric current
stress is anxiety or strain

explanation.surface: Worry follows when a crazy person marries a current head of a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' suggests a madman but is slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A headmistress is the female head teacher of a school, a leader in education.

clue.text: Bathing suit — big kind — is missing bottoms

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its last letter, so each of the three words loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A large swimming costume with its lower half lost, a bathing mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: BIG, KIND and IS each lose their final letter (G, D, S), giving BI, KIN and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit worn by women, a type of bathing suit.

clue.text: Fasten on wooden pin

parts.note: to peg is to fasten, as with clothes pegs
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: An instruction to secure something on a wooden peg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A peg leg is a wooden artificial leg, so it can be jokingly called a wooden pin, pin being slang for leg.

clue.text: Relative's very new and fashionable act

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
in means fashionable, as in the in thing
an act of parliament is a law

explanation.surface: A family member's behaviour is very modern and stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act' suggests behaviour, but means a statute.
explanation.definitionFit: One's daughter's husband is a relation by marriage, so he is a relative.

clue.text: Small child's bed we reduced by 50% for writer

parts.note: a crib is a cot, a baby's bed

indicators.note: halving the two-letter word leaves a single letter, here the second half

explanation.surface: A tiny cot that we have cut in half, offered to someone who writes.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe was a professional copyist of documents, so a writer by trade.

clue.text: Some remote village lifted ban

indicators.note: in a down entry lifted means raised, so the hidden letters read upwards
some means a part of, so the letters lie hidden inside the words

explanation.surface: Part of an isolated village has had a prohibition removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' looks like a ban being removed but reverses the letters upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is the right to forbid or block a decision, a kind of ban.

clue.text: Garibaldi biscuit enthrals bird

indicators.note: enthrals means holds captive, so the words hold the answer within

explanation.surface: A currant biscuit captivates a feathered visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: A Garibaldi is a British biscuit with a currant filling.
explanation.definitionFit: An ibis is a wading bird with a long down-curved bill.

clue.text: 'I can' belief extraordinarily advantageous

indicators.note: extraordinarily means in an unusual manner, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A can-do attitude is remarkably helpful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beneficial brings benefit or good results, so it is favourable and advantageous.

clue.text: Nearly the end of the day? Nearly

indicators.note: nearly means almost all, so the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: night is when the day ends

explanation.surface: A question about nearly the close of the day, answered with nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Nearly' trims NIGHT; the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old word for near or almost, so it can mean nearly.

clue.text: Adult making a noise around front of tavern, staggering

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for making a noise goes around the letter

parts.note: sounding means making a sound or noise

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A grown-up making a racket outside a pub, reeling about drunkenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering' paints a drunk lurching about but means amazing.
explanation.definitionFit: Astounding means amazing or shocking, the same sense as staggering when used of surprising news.
